title: kosha dataset -> meso-discipline assignments (reviewed seed)
description: Maps each kosha registered dataset (data/manifest/datasets.json) to a meso_code of the estate's ratified Russian-Indology meso vocabulary (IndologyScholars curation/meso_discipline_crosswalk.csv vocabulary). The discipline taxonomy itself is NEVER re-derived here (H3567 ruling F5, released by F5c): the build joins these assignments through the crosswalk to curation/disciplines.csv. Confidence is the assignment's own; it multiplies with the crosswalk's confidence downstream. null meso_code = no confident facet in the meso vocabulary; these stay unassigned instead of being forced.
assignmentNote: General Sanskrit lexicography has no dedicated meso code; the nearest Sanskrit facet is sanskrit_grammar_panini (crosswalk target sanskritology, ratified scope 'Vedic studies, Sanskrit grammar, Sanskrit texts and epic'). Those assignments carry confidence <= 0.6 deliberately, per the csl-atlas precedent (dict_meso_assignments.json, H4178). Datasets whose subject is a specific TEXT take the text's facet (Gita/Nala/MBh -> epic_ramayana_mahabharata; Hitopadesa/Kiratarjuniya/subhashita -> literary_studies); datasets whose subject is a linguistic PHENOMENON (sandhi, morphology, paradigms, Panini) take the grammar facet even when sourced from one text. MT-eval, teaching-census and org-process artifacts have no facet at all and stay honest nulls.
